prompt:
Use case: logo-brand. Create one finished Julia lettered logo, an authentic 18th-century printer's device, trade card or engraved shop label. Landscape 1536×1024 PNG, 3:2 aspect ratio. Transparent background.
Design: A bookplate-style framed panel with engraved corner ornaments. The name "Julia" in elaborate but readable copperplate script, and the exact inscription "Est. 1961" beneath in small-capital styling.
Exact lettering: Julia; Est. 1961. Spell Julia J-u-l-i-a, or J-U-L-I-A for roman capitals. No extra words, pseudoletters, signatures or watermark. For dates use exactly Est. 1961 with the period and those four digits.
Medium: eighteenth-century copperplate LINE engraving. Fine crisp cross-hatching, parallel burin strokes, delicate tapering ornamental linework, intentionally engraved hand-lettering integrated into the plate composition. Letters are the identity, not ordinary typeset text added to an illustration. Clear legibility comes before flourishes.
Ink: exclusively umber #2e2119. No other colour, no watercolour wash, no tinted areas, no opaque white or cream interiors, no fill colour, no painted shading. All unprinted spaces including within the device are transparent. Shade through fine separate hatch lines only. Flat lighting, no cast shadows, no paper texture or background. No realistic product render, no ingredient-icon illustration, no soft painterly colour, no modern generic font.
Composition: centered complete design with breathing room, all flourishes and edges inside the canvas. Strong typographic hierarchy and a recognisable silhouette. One design only.
visual_lettering_check: Passed by direct inspection of final artwork.
